key_insight: CGMap uses distance-resolved graph learning to turn dispersed cancer-related signals into an interpretable ranking of candidate genes. This helps researchers focus on promising genes for practical validation.
problem_solved: Cancer-related signals are dispersed, making it difficult to prioritize candidate genes and explain why particular genes warrant experimental follow-up.
method: Apply CGMap, a distance-resolved graph-learning framework, to organize cancer-related signals.
Map these signals into structured gene priorities to narrow the candidate space.
Provide an interpretable path from gene hypotheses to practical validation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, CGMap illustrates how graph learning can support interpretable prioritization in biomedical research. Its focus is on actionable candidate selection rather than prediction alone.
visual_elements: Gene-network diagram with highlighted cancer-related signals and distance layers.
Workflow: dispersed signals → CGMap → ranked genes → experimental validation.
Priority funnel showing a broad candidate pool narrowing to a focused shortlist.
Conceptual explanation panel linking a prioritized gene to supporting network signals.
paper_title: Interpretable distance-resolved graph learning for cancer gene priority screening
paper_authors: Chenhao Wang, Shidong Xu, Li Tang, Gang Luo, Yongchang Zhang
